text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A parliament committee has decided to launch a criminal action against deputy Valdis Krisbergs.
- Prosecutor Igor Yupatov has finished his charge against underworld criminal Ivan Haritonov and asked that he should be sentenced to 8-12 years imprisonment.

- President Guntis Ulmanis is on a visit to Denmark. Speaking at the Danish Foreign Policy Society, Ulmanis stressed that the doors of NATO should not be closed after the first stage of its expansion.
- The artists of the national opera warn that they will go on strike as of April 4 unless their salaries are increased.
- A long interview with Prime Minister Andris Shkele.

- Shareholders of Unibanka are due to decide on merging with the Latvian Zemes banka at an extraordinary meeting on April 21. They are also expected to consider issuing bonds worth of $50 million, according to unofficial sources. The bonds will be distributed on Europe's financial markets. Their interest rate, which is expected to range between 1.0 - 1.5 percent, is likely to be attached to LIBOR.
- Shkele is to meet with major foreign investors at a round table organised by Latvia's Stability Foundation.

- The editor of DB, Juris Paiders, believes that the national currency, lats, is likely to be revalued. One of the reasons he cites is that foreign investors are keen to buy lat bonds yielding three to 4.5 percent annual interest rates instead of investing dollars at 5.18-5.61 percent a year.
